en.title: H2D: OrcaSlicer nightly files fail with "Filament Track Switch offline"
en.body: Files sliced for the H2D with the OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 nightly fail about 2 minutes into the print with HMS 0700-7400 and 0700-8029 ("This print requires a Filament Track Switch") on printers without the switch. This happens whether you print from Bambuddy or from OrcaSlicer itself.

en.title: H2/X2-series / P2S: why some archives only show a name
en.body:
If your archive cards have a name and timing but no thumbnail, filament
total or cost, this is why — and there's a fix that works today.

Bambu Studio's Print button sends sliced files to the printer's
internal memory on H2C, H2D and P2S. Bambuddy reads files off the
printer over FTP, which only serves the SD card or USB stick, so there's
nothing there to fetch. The printer's "Store sent files on external
storage" option does not change it — I measured all three printers with
it enabled, plus an X1C for comparison, which went to the card and
archived fine.

Three ways to get complete archives, easiest first:

- Start the print from Bambuddy
- Slice in OrcaSlicer — it always uploads to the card
- Staying in Studio: use Send with External picked, then start the print from the printer, Handy, or Studio's device page. Print itself offers no storage choice.

All three need a card or stick in the printer. X1 and P1 series are
unaffected.

Also fixed in the next daily: a bug of mine where a print started from a
file already on the stick was treated as internal storage and archived
without its data. That one hit every model, so if you've seen empty
archives on an X1 or P1 recently, this was it.

Details: https://wiki.bambuddy.cool/reference/troubleshooting/#archive-card-has-only-a-name
Upstream: https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/10481
